# v0.9.8 - Snapshots Are of the Whole Repository

## What's Changed in v0.9.8

This release fixes `git seafile-snapshot` when it is run from a subfolder of a repository. Nothing in how a snapshot or a push is stored changes.

### Fixed

- **A snapshot run from a subfolder no longer lands on the repository's vault.** The source's `seafile://` remote was found through the enclosing repository, so the folder's files were committed on top of the whole repository's `-vault` chain (seen as a diff of thousands of deleted files). A snapshot is now of the whole repository, as `git push` is: from a subfolder the source becomes the repository root, with a note, and an explicit `--source` naming a subfolder is refused with the root named. A vault that already remembers a subfolder as its source keeps working. Deriving the vault's destination from the code remote now requires the source to be the repository root.

### Upgrading

If you ran `git seafile-snapshot` from a subfolder before this release and let it derive the destination, the remote vault's branch has a snapshot of that folder as its tip. History is intact; the next snapshot taken from the repository root goes on top of it. The local `<folder>-vault` it created beside the folder can be deleted.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
